summary: On the TCP transport a cleanly departing node hands its ledger pages to their successors before GOODBYE (mxfs_dlm_handoff_depart); pages it could NOT prepare (a target it could not name) are documented as 'finished by the successor's takeover on GOODBYE' — but that takeover needs the departed node's incarnation, the GOODBYE message carries none, and the survivor's heartbeat-slot lookup (find_node_slot + slot_node_cb) answered 0 on the rig 70 times. Those pages stay ACTIVE/PREPARED under a departed authority that no survivor can name: every request on every resource of such a page parks (REMASTER / prepare -EAGAIN) until 'the next survivor that can name it' — which never comes once the slot is released. Availability stall for a whole ledger page (31 resources) per stranded page, unbounded.
mechanism: dlm/v5_mount.c: clean departure = release_all -> mxfs_dlm_handoff_depart (P-TAUTH-DEPART-LEFT pages=N when a successor incarnation cannot be named) -> NODE_LEAVE broadcast (struct mxfs_dlm_node_msg: name/port/volume_id only) -> lease stop -> heartbeat slot release. Receiver (v5_peer_msg_cb_tcp MXFS_MSG_NODE_LEAVE): goodbye_inc from mxfs_disklock_find_node_slot + v5_slot_node_cb (in-memory node_track / platter read) -> v5_handoff_takeover(sender, goodbye_inc, 'goodbye') -> if inc==0: P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER-NOINC and return. Why the lookup is 0 on the rig: NOT yet root-caused (candidates: node_track already cleared by the clean-depart confirm arm or the slot already released by the time the TCP message is processed; find_node_slot's cached slot_node_id[] stale). The fix does not depend on which: the departing node KNOWS its incarnation.
